name: Joseph
overview: Joseph was the eleventh-born son of Jacob and Rachel, a male figure noted in Scripture for his significant role in God's providential plan. Though his tribe is not specified, his identity as the favored son of Rachel marks him as a central character in the Genesis narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Joseph means "he will add," reflecting a hopeful and God-ordained increase, as recorded in Genesis 30:24. Later, he is given the Egyptian name Zaphenath-paneah, which likely means "god speaks, he lives," indicating his elevated status in Egypt as noted in Genesis 41:45.
familyAndRelationships: Joseph is explicitly identified as the son of Jacob and Rachel. He has many half-brothers, including Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah, as well as a full brother, Benjamin. He is also the husband of Asenath, an Egyptian woman given to him during his rise to power.
scriptureSignificance: Joseph's life illustrates God's sovereign hand in elevating the humble and fulfilling His promises. Despite suffering betrayal and slavery at the hands of his brothers, God raised Joseph to a position of authority in Egypt, enabling him to save many from famine. His story prefigures Christ through themes of suffering, exaltation, and redemption, demonstrating grace and forgiveness that align with God's redemptive plan.

keyEvents.event: Sold into slavery by his brothers
